Scott,

It seems strange that dplyr says it depends on Rcpp >= 0.10.6, but looks like it works with 0.10.5 on your machine. Either way, I'm glad to hear it's working. Please reach out if you run into

I am using mac system(10.9.1) and my R version is 3.0.2. My rstudio is also most up-to-dated. Could anyone solve this problem?

I am looking into this issue. It's clear that the size of this package is breaking things, but it's not clear if this is a bug with ShinyApps, or a limitation/issue with GitHub.

Side note: It's usually considered a bad idea to have such large binary files in a Git repository. Unfortunately, only CRAN and GitHub packages are supported at the moment for ShinyApps.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] speed issues
messages.body_plain:
Michael,

I believe this is UTF-8 encoding problem. If I check the javascript console when I load your app I see:

Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token N shiny.js:764 <http://mlgi.shinyapps.io/protest/shared/shiny.js>
dispatchMessageshiny.js:764 <http://mlgi.shinyapps.io/protest/shared/shiny.js>
socket.onmessageshiny.js:491 <http://mlgi.shinyapps.io/protest/shared/shiny.js>
d.dispatchEventsockjs-0.3.min.js:27 <http://mlgi.shinyapps.io/protest/__assets__/sockjs-0.3.min.js>
y._dispatchMessagesockjs-0.3.min.js:27 <http://mlgi.shinyapps.io/protest/__assets__/sockjs-0.3.min.js>
y._didMessagesockjs-0.3.min.js:27 <http://mlgi.shinyapps.io/protest/__assets__/sockjs-0.3.min.js>
e.ws.onmessage

If I recall correctly, this can be caused by the fact that ShinyApps by default is not using a UTF-8 encoding, and your app is attempting to read UTF-8 encoded data.

This is obviously an issue with ShinyApps that we need to fix. However the work around right now is to add a file to your application called ".Renviron". That file should have the text:

LANG="C.UTF-8"

messages.body_plain:
Josh,

It looks like something very strange is going on with the description for that version of the 'jpeg' package. I just confirmed locally that it is missing the "Repository: CRAN" field that we use to detect if the package is installed from CRAN. This is pretty unusual, and it may be worthwhile reaching out to the package maintainer.

A work around may be use a older version of the package, using install_version from the devtools package:

devtools::install_version('jpeg', '0.1-6')

-Andy

I just wanted to give you an update.  I wasn't able to get an older version of the package to work, so I contacted the package maintainer. He believes the issue on your end, because the "Repository" isn't a documented field. For my purposes, I was able to use .png file instead and read it in with the PNG package.  This worked without any issues.

Thanks again for your help!
Josh

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Limits to Shiny Server
messages.body_plain:
There is currently no limit on the amount of disk space that can be used. However, this is likely to change. We will enforce some type of limit in the coming months. However please keep in mind that data written to application instances <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md#application-instances> is not persisted, or durable in any way.

messages.subject: Resolved: 502 Errors
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

Some users have reported errors deploying their applications, and other users have reporter 502 errors when trying to access their applications. I have identified some issues with one of our servers this evening. The underlying issues have been resolved, however some users may need to re-deploy their applications using deployApp(). The fastest way do this is:

deployApp(upload=FALSE)

This will reboot your application without re-uploading.

If you are still having trouble deploying your application, or you are seeing a 502 errors, and re-deploying does not fix it, please post an message to the discussion list.

Sorry for the trouble, and thanks for bearing with us while work out the kinks with ShinyApps.

-Andy

Should I refer to the file in a different way or my guess is wrong and the issue is completely independent on that? I will greatly appreciate any help. If you need more information about my app, don't hesitate to request.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to add user authentication and password protection to a tool that I am building. I am going by the method outlined in this page : https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md

I am getting the following error on using the function :
"Error in hashPassword(password) :
  function 'enterRNGScope' not provided by package 'Rcpp' "

On further inspection, I found that maybe there is something wrong with the most updated version of Rcpp package (Rcpp v 0.11.0). I tried solving it with some solutions off the web but it screwed my whole app. Is anybody else facing a similar problem ? Can anybody help me rectify it ? This is very important as my client would not allow this tool to be used without password protection and this is the only sticking point. Really greatful for any help.

Thanks a lot,
Ameek Singh

messages.subject: Re: Authentication - scrypt package install issue.
messages.body_plain:
Josh,

I think you're hitting an issue with OSX Mavericks using a different compiler then R was compiled with (clang vs llvm). See this <https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/36> and this <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/20572535/error-in-dyn-load-in-rcpp-package-in-mac> for more info if you're interested.

The work around is to install Rcpp from source using this command:

install.packages('Rcpp', type='source')

and then:

devtools::install_github('rstudio/rscrypt')

Let me know if that works!

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I recently uploaded my ShinyApp to the Shiny server. No errors were reported during the deployment of the application, and the process completed successfully.

However, when I ran my application, I noticed that functions do not run and instead print the message that, for example, "could not find function getURL". Additionally, I had specified the tabSetPanels to update themselves based on different user choices, but they too have no effect.

Here is the link to my application: https://aliakazmi.shinyapps.io/QualitativeAnalysisApp-R/
Here is the link to my code: https://github.com/noobuseR/QualitativeAnalysisApp-R

Thanks in advance for any advise/assistance.

Kind Regards.
AA

Can you paste the output of that command here?

library(shiny)
library(fastcluster)
etc...

And then re-run deployApp().

Let me know the result.

-Andy

That solves the problem for libraries. Thank you.

But there is another problem I am facing now: some of the commands return error messages and don't work as expected. For examples, I am unable to upload files, some functions from the tm package generate error, and Javascript seems to crash sometimes. It is strange because everything works perfectly fine locally.

Once again, thanks for the hard work you put into ShinyApps!

messages.subject: ShinyApp unexpectedly exits (seemingly when a large dataset uploaded)
messages.subject_clean: ShinyApp unexpectedly exits (seemingly when a large dataset uploaded)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working on an application which should allow users to upload data and then do some textual analysis thereof.
Here is what I want to achieve:

1. Allow users to upload text dataset using any from the list provided, or from their local space.
2. Perform pre-processing of the dataset.
3. To generate features from the dataset.
...

But I face errors in 2) and 3). The errors are such that:

i. Sometimes they occur, sometimes do not occur (though it appears to me the error occurs more often when a large dataset is used. For example, I have 3 datasets - UAE Expat forum, UAE TripAdvisor, and Middle East Politics Forum - and the error occurs more often with the Middle East Politics forum dataset).
ii. Sometimes no error is sent to the Javascript console, sometimes the following

Listening on port 59669
Read 2230 items
Warning in parallel::mclapply(x, FUN, ...) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
Warning in parallel::mclapply(x, FUN, ...) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code

The above occurs when the pre-processing phase fails and the application exits unexpectedly.

Warning in parallel::mclapply(x, FUN, ...) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
Warning in parallel::mclapply(x, FUN, ...) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
Warning in parallel::mclapply(x, termFreq, control) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
Warning in is.na(x) :
  is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
Warning in TermDocumentMatrix.VCorpus(preprocessedCorpus(), control = list(weighting = function(x) weightSMART(x,  :
  invalid document identifiers
Warning in simple_triplet_matrix(i = i, j = j, v = as.numeric(v), nrow = length(allTerms),  :
  NAs introduced by coercion
Error in simple_triplet_matrix(i = i, j = j, v = as.numeric(v), nrow = length(allTerms),  :
  'i, j, v' different lengths
Error in simple_triplet_matrix(i = i, j = j, v = as.numeric(v), nrow = length(allTerms),  :
  'i, j, v' different lengths

The above occurs when the pre-processing phase is accomplished, but the feature generation phase results in an error. The above error must not occur as I have tested the same code locally, and it works fine each time I try.

I have also noticed shiny-server-pro.js <https://aliakazmi.shinyapps.io/sampleTextAnalysisApp/__assets__/shiny-server-pro.js> in the console, but I am afraid I don't know if that is relevant.

Here is the link to my app: https://aliakazmi.shinyapps.io/sampleTextAnalysisApp/
Here is the link to the ui.R file: https://gist.github.com/noobuseR/711a39df5ce16e0093e6#file-ui-r
Here is the link to the server.R file: https://gist.github.com/noobuseR/711a39df5ce16e0093e6#file-server-r

Please do let me know if there is more I can do to assist in the process of solving this problem.

Kind Regards,
AK

messages.subject: My Google Analytics Shinyapp
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone, thanks to the help of this forum I've got a Shinyapp up and running, it uses Google Analytics data to do some forecasting etc.  Hopefully more to come, but I put the app itself here:
https://mark.shinyapps.io/GA_timeseries/

....and a blog post around it here:
http://markedmondson.me/my-google-analytics-time-series-shiny-app-alpha

Some extra details for shinyappers:
I'd like to be able to update the menu's using updateSelectInput() rather than renderUI() that I had to use instead. Just couldn't get select functions to work
The new dataTableOutput() got me out of a hole trying to update the rows of the tables based on the inputs, I love it :)
I have to do a hard refresh sometimes if it unauthenticates users, I'd like a more sophisticated way to handle that within the app itself.
I've realised a lot of work is in dealing with null outputs or errors, I'd like to be able to set some kind of default output for every table
I'm not sure on the bandwidth/processing limits of shinyapps?  I think I'll need some limits of datafetches to prevent hangups.
I couldn't get rCharts to play nicely and display graphs easily, in the end googleVis() got used as it was the easiest to get output working, but I'd prefer a d3 or Highcharts option.
Still not sure how to make the data fetch only perform once per profile, meaning lots of unnecessary GA API calls, I think isolate() may be needed but with some kind of time lag?
Yours sincerely,
Mark

I am not sure if you are aware of the shiny-discuss discussion list <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shiny-discuss> where there may be a lot more people who could help give you ideas for how to get around Shiny's limitation and where our engineers who are focused on Shiny are constantly listening for opportunities to make Shiny easier to use.
As for the authentication restart comment, we totally hear you, and appreciate what you are trying to do.  Ideally adding and removing users should not touch any of the running containers.  We are just missing some of the needed capabilities within Shiny Server Pro to allow us to seamlessly add and remove users. Once that is in place, we will look at incorporating those capabilities within ShinyApps.

Best,

-Tareef

Hi,

The problem you describe sounds like it could be because your application instance is running out of memory. I would suggest reading the Application Instances section of the guide <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md#application-instances>, and trying increasing your instance since to a larger type.

-Andy

I've also come to conclude that 256MB of memory is probably too small for a lot of people's apps. We may make the default 512MB from now on.

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
John,

I spent a little bit of time digging into this more. I was mistaking here, this crash is not actually related to rlimits what-so-ever. What I think is going on here is that internally the underlying scrypt functions for calculating SHA256 hashes have the same names as the OpenSSL functions for doing SHA256 hashes (this is copied from the base scrypt) utility. When running R from the command line, this is not really an issue because R does not link against OpenSSL:

$ ldd /usr/lib/R/bin/exec/R
linux-vdso.so.1 =>  (0x00007fff465ff000)
libR.so => /usr/lib/libR.so (0x00007f3ac7e9e000)
libgomp.so.1 => /usr/lib/libgomp.so.1 (0x00007f3ac7c90000)
libpthread.so.0 => /lib/libpthread.so.0 (0x00007f3ac7a72000)
libc.so.6 => /lib/libc.so.6 (0x00007f3ac76eb000)
libblas.so.3gf => /usr/lib/atlas/libblas.so.3gf (0x00007f3ac6d50000)
libgfortran.so.3 => /usr/lib/libgfortran.so.3 (0x00007f3ac6a62000)
libm.so.6 => /lib/libm.so.6 (0x00007f3ac67df000)
libreadline.so.6 => /lib/libreadline.so.6 (0x00007f3ac659e000)
liblzma.so.1 => /usr/lib/liblzma.so.1 (0x00007f3ac637c000)
librt.so.1 => /lib/librt.so.1 (0x00007f3ac6174000)
libdl.so.2 => /lib/libdl.so.2 (0x00007f3ac5f70000)
/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007f3ac8460000)
libgcc_s.so.1 => /lib/libgcc_s.so.1 (0x00007f3ac5d58000)
libncurses.so.5 => /lib/libncurses.so.5 (0x00007f3ac5b15000)

However the rsession process within RStudio Server does:

$ ldd /usr/local/lib/rstudio/bin/rsession
linux-vdso.so.1 =>  (0x00007fff2ddff000)
libR.so => /usr/lib/libR.so (0x00007f84affc2000)
libpthread.so.0 => /lib/libpthread.so.0 (0x00007f84afda5000)
libutil.so.1 => /lib/libutil.so.1 (0x00007f84afba1000)
libuuid.so.1 => /lib/libuuid.so.1 (0x00007f84af99c000)
librt.so.1 => /lib/librt.so.1 (0x00007f84af794000)
libz.so.1 => /lib/libz.so.1 (0x00007f84af57c000)
libssl.so.0.9.8 => /lib/libssl.so.0.9.8 (0x00007f84af328000)
libcrypto.so.0.9.8 => /lib/libcrypto.so.0.9.8 (0x00007f84aef97000)
libpam.so.0 => /lib/libpam.so.0 (0x00007f84aed89000)
libdl.so.2 => /lib/libdl.so.2 (0x00007f84aeb85000)
libm.so.6 => /lib/libm.so.6 (0x00007f84ae902000)
libc.so.6 => /lib/libc.so.6 (0x00007f84ae57a000)
/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007f84b0584000)
libblas.so.3gf => /usr/lib/atlas/libblas.so.3gf (0x00007f84adbdf000)
libgfortran.so.3 => /usr/lib/libgfortran.so.3 (0x00007f84ad8f2000)
libreadline.so.6 => /lib/libreadline.so.6 (0x00007f84ad6b0000)
liblzma.so.1 => /usr/lib/liblzma.so.1 (0x00007f84ad48f000)
libgomp.so.1 => /usr/lib/libgomp.so.1 (0x00007f84ad281000)
libcrypt.so.1 => /lib/libcrypt.so.1 (0x00007f84ad047000)
libgcc_s.so.1 => /lib/libgcc_s.so.1 (0x00007f84ace30000)
libncurses.so.5 => /lib/libncurses.so.5 (0x00007f84acbec000)

When running the scrypt functions from within an rsession you get the following crash:

#0  0x00007ffa2936c53b in memcpy () from /lib/libc.so.6
#1  0x00007ffa29d7436f in SHA256_Update () from /lib/libcrypto.so.0.9.8
#2  0x00007ffa1d8714cf in PBKDF2_SHA256 (passwd=0x0, passwdlen=0, salt=<value optimized out>,
    saltlen=<value optimized out>, c=1, buf=<value optimized out>, dkLen=128) at scrypt-1.1.6/lib/crypto/sha256.c:386
#3  0x00007ffa1d8725ff in crypto_scrypt (passwd=<value optimized out>, passwdlen=<value optimized out>, salt=0x0,
    saltlen=0, N=<value optimized out>, r=<value optimized out>, p=1, buf=0x0, buflen=0)
    at scrypt-1.1.6/lib/crypto/crypto_scrypt-ref.c:258
#4  0x00007ffa1d877970 in getcpuperf (opps=0x7fffeabb6cd0) at util.cpp:147
#5  0x00007ffa1d8760d1 in getparams (passwd=..., maxmem=<value optimized out>, maxtime=<value optimized out>)
    at scrypt.cpp:49
#6  hashPassword (passwd=..., maxmem=<value optimized out>, maxtime=<value optimized out>) at scrypt.cpp:129
#7  0x00007ffa1d873a7a in scrypt_hashPassword (passwdSEXP=0x51c0038, maxmemSEXP=0x5dbe948, maxtimeSEXP=0x5dbe9a8)
    at RcppExports.cpp:18

Which shows that the SHA256_Update() from libcrypto (OpenSSL) is being called instead of the function from the scrypt library, which is likely causing the crash.

I will work on fix (the simplest thing to do is to just rename the functions).

Thanks for the bug report John.
-Andy

What I think is going on here is that internally the underlying scrypt functions for calculating SHA256 hashes have the same names as the OpenSSL functions for doing SHA256 hashes (this is copied from the base scrypt) utility. messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] installing packages from github
messages.body_plain:
Ajay,

So I understand correctly, are you trying to install this package from your application code (ui.R or server.R)? If that is the case, you do not need to do that. In fact it is not allowed.

ShinyApps will automatically detect which packages your application depends on, and installs those packages automatically on the server when you call deployApp().

-Andy
